**Triage: lands in `packages/plugin-charts/src/normalizeChartSchema.ts` (`label()`); `domain:ui`; `priority:p2`.**

```ts
if (isRec(v)) {
  const first = Object.values(v).find((x) => typeof x === 'string' && x);
  return first as string | undefined;
}
```

The inline-locale-map arm returns **the first string value in key order**, so a chart heading follows however the object literal happened to be written rather than the viewer's language. ⇒ a user with a language set can be shown another language's heading, deterministically and silently.

⇒ p2: wrong-language output is user-visible, and there is no diagnostic — the chart renders confidently in the wrong locale.

⚠️ **Use the repo's existing locale resolution rather than writing a second one.** A module-local `label()` that hand-rolls locale picking is how this class recurs; if a shared resolver exists (the sibling readers of localized values use one), route through it. ⭐ If none exists at this layer, say so in the PR — "there was no shared resolver" is a real finding and better than quietly minting a third implementation.

⛔ Not in scope: objectui#7946 / PR #8884's ruled key set, which the filing seat correctly kept separate.

`Size/model suggestion:` S–M.

Clause-②: yes

### Why yes — and why the route does not change it

Measured on `origin/main` `681d3f10e`, controls lit: **`normalizeChartSchema` is a published export** — `packages/plugin-charts/src/index.tsx:32` is `export { normalizeChartSchema } from './normalizeChartSchema';`, with its `NormalizedChartSchema` type beside it on line 33.

The card offers two routes and I deliberately left the choice to the implementer. Both land on the published surface:

- **Route 1** (thread the active language in as a parameter) changes the **signature** of a published function.
- **Route 2** (leave normalisation locale-free, resolve at the render site) changes what that published function **returns** for a locale-map `title`.

⇒ The declaration is `yes` either way, so the implementer is not choosing the review posture by choosing the route.

⚠️ Note what is **not** the reason: the accept set does not widen. `@objectstack/spec` already types this slot as `I18nLabel` — a string **or** an inline locale map — so the map arm is authored surface today and stays exactly as admissible. This card makes the code match a contract that already says locale-aware resolution; it does not move the contract. The `yes` rests on the published function, not on the authored key.

### Who reviews

Per objectstack-ai/objectstack#17285 the contract-review tier is **not** this lane's: this lane runs the default tier for both build and review, and the lane seat's own default-tier review plus the gates is the review of record. The Clause-② review owed here will be an in-seat one, posted on the delivering PR — same handling as objectui#9019, objectui#9016 and objectui#9028 this session.

### ⚠️ C3, disclosed up front rather than discovered later

`check-clause2-carriers` fires **C3** on a pair that declares `yes` while `needs:contract-review` is hung on neither carrier. I am not hanging it, for a measured reason: **no workflow in objectui reads that label** (checked with the control lit — it is PM tooling state, not a CI gate), and per objectstack#17285 the tier it summons does not serve this lane at all, so hanging it would bind the door to a reviewer who does not exist here. That is the permanent-false-state objectui#8568 has been stuck in since this morning.

⇒ Recorded openly, not routed around. This is the **third** instance of one governance question this session (objectui#8568, objectui#8973, this card) and it goes to the maintainer as a group. ⛔ This seat is not resolving it in either direction, and ⛔ is not clearing anything.

### Dispatch note — two of my own assumptions, already answered so the dev need not re-derive them

- **`@object-ui/i18n` is already a declared dependency** of `@object-ui/plugin-charts` (`workspace:*`, `package.json:36`) ⇒ routing through `pickLocalized` adds **no** new dependency edge, so the manual-floor stop I fenced does not apply.
- `label(` appears **6** times in a 629-line `normalizeChartSchema.ts`, so "every caller" is a real population and not a single site — the ledger-by-name requirement in the dispatch has teeth.
